prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: advisory decision support for WUI wildfire detection/suppression. Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (alias Emberhall), primary interface for Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison, command staff; shows camera views, history, weather, maps, state transitions; opens triage case when automated confidence exceeds screening threshold. North and South Lookout Camera Masts: hardened power, lightning protection, licensed wireless video, cellular degraded-mode path; North sends Thermal Spot Snippet on local candidate heat signature. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (alias Kestrel): enclosures, charging, health monitoring, secure network termination; produces Battery Swap Ticket at battery replacement threshold. Drone Tasking Service: approved flight requests, constraints, task status; not flight-release authority; used by Drone Pilot Operator; may prepare verification task for Kestrel when terrain, column height or occlusion blocks fixed-camera view. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (alias Lantern): receives observation context, normalizes image/thermal/weather into common event record; traceable recommendations; retains timing, source IDs, model versions, acknowledgments; score is not a fire declaration. Smoke Classifier Module: scores plume (texture, persistence, motion, contrast), sends confidence to Lantern; produces Ridge Shadow Mask for terrain-shadow conditions. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (alias Brindle): station/forecast ingest, QC; provides wind, humidity, temperature, stability context; sends Wind Shift Bulletin. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater: recorded, access-controlled. Crewline Mobile Tablet: gives Helitack Crew Leader approved incident context, maps, updates. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console: aircraft coordination, loading status, mission notes for Air Attack Supervisor and Tanker Base Manager. East and West Retardant Loading Pumps: monitored assets, readiness/fault visible to authorized staff. Baseline: network segmentation, time sync, health checks, audit logging. Actors: County Emergency Liaison; Duty Detection Officer (alias Orion) reviews triage, compares frames, may request PTZ view, recommends escalation/Confirmed Ignition State only when supported; Air Attack Supervisor; Tanker Base Manager; Helitack Crew Leader; Drone Pilot Operator. Detection flow: masts or dock observation → timestamped, georeferenced, equipment status → Lantern → triage → human review. Thermal cues supporting unless persistent across frames or aligned with smoke. States: suspected ignition, Confirmed Ignition State, Airspace Restricted State. Detection ends when authorized role accepts, rejects or requests

New part:
S063: The Drone Pilot Operator confirms that the proposed verification task is safe for launch conditions and consistent with current operating constraints.
S064: The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater supports voice coordination when field observers or aviation personnel can provide independent confirmation from their location.
S065: The Air Attack Supervisor may be referred to by the alias Redtail during radio coordination, but the operational record uses Air Attack Supervisor.
S066: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console may be referred to by the alias Marigold during dispatch coordination, but the operational record uses Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console.
S067: Confirmation requires at least one persistent smoke indication or thermal cue, plus either independent sensor corroboration, field report corroboration, or a direct human visual judgment recorded by an authorized reviewer.
S068: A suspected ignition remains in triage when evidence is inconsistent, stale, or limited to a single low-confidence source.
S069: The Caldera Incident Command Portal records the reason for each triage decision so later operators can understand whether the case was advanced, held, or dismissed.
S070: When the confirmation rule is satisfied, the incident record is advanced to the Confirmed Ignition State and becomes available for suppression planning.
S071: The Confirmed Ignition State includes the best known location, confidence basis, observation history, reviewer identity, and current recommended coordination posture.
S072: Crewline Mobile Tablet users receive only the confirmed incident context that has been released for field distribution by the command workflow.
S073: East Retardant Loading Pump sends the Retardant Batch Slip after a load cycle is metered and sealed.
S074: If air operations are constrained, the Caldera Incident Command Portal can associate the incident with the Airspace Restricted State before aircraft tasking is attempted.
S075: Dismissed cases remain searchable for audit and model improvement, but they do not create a suppression assignment or public incident notification.
S076: This section defines how the Caldera Incident Command Portal supports coordinated air and ground operations after an incident enters a managed response posture.
S077: When the Caldera Incident Command Portal shows the Airspace Restricted State, aircraft tasking is treated as conditional until the Air Attack Supervisor confirms the active operating window.
S078: The Duty Detection Officer records the restriction basis in the Caldera Incident Command Portal so later decisions can be traced to the operational condition in effect at the time.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
